subject: Clarify: pro‑rata billing windows & minimum credits apportionment
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@atlasanalytics.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@atlasanalytics.com
Date: Thu, 15 Nov 2028 09:04:00 -0500
Subject: Quick question on pro‑rata windows and minimum credits

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the pricing walkthrough yesterday. A procurement question came up when we walked the draft SOW through legal: how do you apportion the monthly minimums and pro‑rata usage when our seat pool is shared across two clusters with shifted timezone schedules? Two concrete scenarios:

1) A seat is active for 6 days in month A and 24 days in month B (moved mid‑billing cycle). Do we receive a simple day‑weighted proration of the monthly seat credit, or is it applied to the usage buckets?

2) We batch long contexts at night and short contexts during the day; for nights we often hit the context‑length minimum and during the day we fall below it. Are minimums evaluated per request, per session, or aggregated per seat per rolling window?

If you have a short example spreadsheet that shows the math end‑to‑end, that would help us close this internally.

Also attaching the draft slot allocation to show how our seats move between clusters.

Best,
Sanjay
Procurement, Atlas Analytics

Attachments: slot_allocation.pdf (pdf)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@atlasanalytics.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Nov 2028 10:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Quick question on pro‑rata windows and minimum credits

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the clear examples, that helps. Short answer: we use a deterministic, time‑weighted apportionment for seat credits and a rolling window aggregation for minimums so you don’t get double‑charged when contexts vary. Below I sketched the approach and attached a tiny worked example (pro_rata_examples.csv).

1) Seat credit proration: monthly reserved seat credits are prorated by active days on a per‑seat basis (day‑weighted). If Seat A is owned 6 days in Nov and 24 days in Dec, each month receives the seat credit only for the days the seat was assigned. We do not split the credit across seats unless the seat has been partially used by multiple accounts in the same billing org.

Example (simplified): monthly-seat-credit = $100 / 30 days = $3.333/day. Nov: 6 days * 3.333 = $19.998 ; Dec: 24 days * 3.333 = $79.992.

2) Minimums and context length: minimum billing floors are evaluated against an aggregation window per customer route (default = 1h rolling). Within that window, we sum billable units (post‑tokenization) across all requests for the route and then apply minimums (and rounding) at the window level. Practically this prevents you from paying the floor multiple times for a set of short requests that collectively exceed the floor.

We also expose a per‑route override for customers that prefer per‑request minimums (not recommended for bursty micro‑requests).

I attached a spreadsheet column that shows night batch vs day micro‑requests aggregated over the 1h window and the resulting billed units. Note the KV cache reuse reduces billed tokens on repeated context prefixes — the spreadsheet shows a column for that effect.

If this aligns with your expectations, I can convert the example into the numbers you can drop into legal. Vanessa / Mina — any additional constraints around seat transfers or contract language we should surface?

Cheers,
Jonas
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pro_rata_examples.csv (csv), pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Quick question on pro‑rata windows and minimum credits

Quick internal note before we finalize: two contract drafting suggestions —

• Define "active day" precisely (UTC midnight cutoff vs. local timezone). Recommend UTC to keep billing deterministic across relocations.
• Add an examples appendix showing both the day‑weighted seat proration and the 1h rolling window aggregation with at least one example where KV cache reduces billed tokens. That reduces back‑and‑forth during procurement reviews.

Mina — can you run the spreadsheet with UTC day boundaries and include a sample clause for the appendix? I'll review for commercial language.

—Vanessa
Sr. Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@atlasanalytics.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Nov 2028 15:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Quick question on pro‑rata windows and minimum credits

Hi all — attaching the UTC‑aligned examples and a short clause you can paste into the SOW. I preserved your original numbers and added a second worked case for a seat that migrates mid‑month and is shared 50/50 between two clusters for three days. Summary highlights:

• Seat proration: "Active day" is defined as any calendar day (UTC) where seat assignment exists for a customer; credits are charged on a per‑day basis at (monthly_credit / days_in_month) and rounded to the cent.
• Window aggregation: For minimums we aggregate billed units over a 1 hour rolling window per route. If aggregated units < minimum, we bill up to the minimum once per window. If aggregated units >= minimum, we bill actual units. Rounding: billed units are rounded to the nearest whole billing quantum (our implementation default is 10 token quantum for embeddings/units and 1 token for completions).

I included a small table showing the numerical rounding and a worked example where KV cache reduces billable input by 40% for repeated prefixes during the night batch.

Sanjay — let me know if you want me to prepare a one‑page summary for legal that we can drop into the contract.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Pricing & Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachments: pro_rata_examples_UTC.csv (csv), clause_text.docx (docx)
